source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which client is at greatest risk for folic acid deficiency anemia?
questions.rationale: Risks include alcoholism, pregnancy, low intake of uncooked vegetables, and malabsorption.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Folic Acid Deficiency (PDF p. 299)
questions.quote: Alcoholism

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The usual oral dose of folic acid for folate deficiency anemia is:
questions.rationale: Folic acid 1 mg daily; IM for malabsorption.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Folic Acid Deficiency (PDF p. 299)
questions.quote: Administer 1mg of folic acid daily

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which antibiotic is linked to aplastic anemia?
questions.rationale: Chloramphenicol, sulfonamides, benzene, radiation, and chemotherapy can cause aplastic anemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aplastic Anemia (PDF p. 299)
questions.quote: Chloramphenicol

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A CBC showing low RBCs, WBCs, and platelets is called:
questions.rationale: Aplastic anemia causes pancytopenia from marrow failure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aplastic Anemia (PDF p. 299)
questions.quote: resulting in pancytopenia (decreased RBCs, WBCs' and platelets

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which nursing measure is appropriate for a client with aplastic anemia?
questions.rationale: Protect from infection and bleeding: reverse isolation, no SQ or IM injections, soft brush, electric razor.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aplastic Anemia (PDF p. 300)
questions.quote: Reverse isolation due leukopenia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which condition triggers sickling of hemoglobin S?
questions.rationale: HbS crystallizes and sickles when oxygen tension is low; dehydration, cold, and infection also trigger it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sickle Cell Anemia (PDF p. 300)
questions.quote: acquires a crystal-like formation when exposed to low oxygen tension

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In sickle cell pain crisis, which nursing action is a priority?
questions.rationale: Treat triggers: hydrate, give oxygen, manage pain, and treat infection; avoid cold.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sickle Cell Management (PDF p. 300)
questions.quote: Dehydration: Infuse intravenous fluids.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease is usually caused by:
questions.rationale: Aplastic crisis results from parvovirus infection; sequestration crisis results from organ pooling.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sickle Cell Crisis (PDF p. 300)
questions.quote: Aplastic crisis - results from infection with the human parvovirus

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A child with thalassemia major receives frequent transfusions. Which therapy prevents iron overload?
questions.rationale: Multiple PRBC transfusions cause iron overload, managed with regular chelation (e.g., deferoxamine).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thalassemia Major (PDF p. 301)
questions.quote: Management: regular chelation therapy

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Thalassemia major is also known as:
questions.rationale: Severe beta-thalassemia is called thalassemia major or Cooley's anemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thalassemia (PDF p. 301)
questions.quote: Severe beta-thalassemia (i.e., thalassemia major or Cooley’s anemia)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a ruddy complexion, pruritus, and splenomegaly has elevated RBCs, WBCs, and platelets. This is:
questions.rationale: Polycythemia vera is a myeloproliferative disorder with elevated cell counts and hyperviscosity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Polycythemia Vera (PDF p. 301)
questions.quote: Ruddy complexion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the primary treatment for polycythemia vera?
questions.rationale: Phlebotomy (initially 500 mL once or twice weekly) reduces blood viscosity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Polycythemia Vera (PDF p. 301)
questions.quote: Phlebotomy – removing enough blood

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which instruction is appropriate for a client with polycythemia vera and pruritus?
options: Bathe in tepid water, pat dry
questions.rationale: Use tepid or cool baths, avoid vigorous toweling, and avoid iron and aspirin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Polycythemia Vera Nursing Care (PDF p. 301)
questions.quote: Bathing in tepid or cool water

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Hemophilia A results from deficiency of factor:
questions.rationale: Hemophilia A: factor VIII; hemophilia B (Christmas disease): factor IX; both X-linked.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemophilia (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: Hemophilia A – caused by genetic disease that results in deficient or defective factor VIII

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is hemophilia seen almost exclusively in males?
questions.rationale: Hemophilia is an X-linked trait; females are usually carriers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemophilia (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: Both types of hemophilia are inherited as X-linked traits, so almost all affected people are males

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Where does most bleeding occur in hemophilia?
questions.rationale: About 75% of bleeding is into joints (hemarthrosis); intracranial bleeding is most dangerous.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemophilia (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: 75% of all bleeding occurs into joints

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which medication should a client with hemophilia avoid for a headache?
questions.rationale: Avoid aspirin, NSAIDs, and herbal supplements; paracetamol is safer.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemophilia Nursing Care (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: Instruct the patient to avoid OTC medications such as aspirin, NSAIDs

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A child with hemophilia has a nosebleed. Which action is inappropriate?
questions.rationale: Nasal packing is avoided because bleeding often resumes when it is removed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemophilia Nursing Care (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: Nasal packing should be avoided

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which layer of the heart is responsible for contraction?
questions.rationale: Myocardium is muscle; endocardium lines chambers and valves; epicardium is outer.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Layers of the Heart (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: Myocardium-made up of muscle fibers and is responsible for the contraction

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Cardiac output is calculated as:
questions.rationale: CO = HR × SV, normally about 5 L/min.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Output (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: Cardiac Output = Heart Rate x Stroke Volume

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: According to Starling's law, increased ventricular filling results in:
questions.rationale: The more the heart fills during diastole, the more forcefully it contracts.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Starling's Law (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: The more the heart is filled during diastole, the more forcefully it contracts

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Increased afterload from severe hypertension causes stroke volume to:
questions.rationale: Higher afterload means more resistance and lower stroke volume.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Afterload (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: The higher the afterload, the lower the stroke volume.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An S3 heart sound in a 60-year-old client most likely indicates:
questions.rationale: S3 suggests heart failure or regurgitation in adults; it may be normal under age 30.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Heart Sounds (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: this can occur in conditions such as congestive heart failure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The heart's natural pacemaker, firing 60–100 bpm, is the:
questions.rationale: SA node 60–100; AV node 40–60; Purkinje 20–40 bpm.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, SA Node (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: Function: Pacemaker of heart

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The QRS complex on an ECG represents:
questions.rationale: P = atrial depolarization; QRS = ventricular depolarization; T = ventricular repolarization.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ECG (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: The QRS complex represents ventricular muscle depolarization

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the normal PR interval?
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ECG (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: normal PR interval is 0.12 to 0.20 seconds.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A prolonged QT interval places the client at risk for:
questions.rationale: Prolonged QT increases risk of lethal ventricular dysrhythmia such as torsades.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, QT Interval (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: If QT interval becomes prolonged, the patient may be at risk for a lethal ventricular dysrhythmia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A prominent U wave on the ECG suggests:
questions.rationale: U waves usually appear when potassium is low.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, U Wave (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: usually it is not seen unless a patient’s potassium level is low (Hypokalemia)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of coronary artery disease?
questions.rationale: Atherosclerosis, abnormal accumulation of fats in arteries, is the most common cause.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Coronary Artery Disease (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: Most common cause of cardiovascular disease is atherosclerosis
